subject: Letter of engagement: runtime interop & tracing co-development
messages:
From: Elijah Stone <elijah@elliot-consulting.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Letter of engagement: runtime interop & tracing co-development

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the intro on last week's call. Elliot Consulting runs integrations and instrumentation work for platform vendors and a number of ISVs; we've sketched a short pilot we think maps tightly to Redwood's runtime and tracing roadmap. High-level scope:

- Instrument LangChain and LlamaIndex SDK flows to emit standardized trace headers (request id, model variant, quantization profile).
- Validate prefix/KV cache handoff semantics so traces correlate across the co-located microservices.
- Build a small runtime shim and a tracer adapter to replay traces against both hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Acceptance: sample workload (3k concurrent short-chat queries), end-to-end trace visualizations, and a short perf delta report.

Attached is a short Letter of Engagement (LoE) that outlines roles, timeline (6 weeks), and a notional resource commitment. Can you confirm interest and whether legal / procurement should review before we schedule a planning session next week?

[Attachment: draft-LoE.pdf (PDF)]

Best,
Elijah Stone
Head of Partnerships, Elliot Consulting
elijah@elliot-consulting.com
+1 (415) 555-0124
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elijah Stone <elijah@elliot-consulting.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Letter of engagement: runtime interop & tracing co-development

Elijah —

Appreciate the clear scope. Redwood is interested in a focused pilot to prove instrumentation compatibility across our hosted and dedicated runtimes. A few quick points from my side:

- We prefer the pilot to target LangChain telemetry first, with a follow-up adapter for LlamaIndex to reduce surface area.
- Security: no customer data should leave our test VPC; traces must be scrubbed of PII and hashed request ids.
- Ops: please list required kernel/runtime hooks up front (KV cache exports, trace emit hook locations).

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal kickoff — Tue 2028-06-27 10:00 PT (30 min)
2) Joint scoping session w/ Eng + CS — Thu 2028-06-29 11:00 PT (60 min)
3) Legal/Procurement loop once we agree on the LoE terms (week of Jul 1).

I've attached an initial scope note that captures the above and a recommended resource plan. Jonas, can your infra PM Priya Natarajan join the scoping call to confirm runtime changes? Vanessa, please flag any marketplace or partner compliance items.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

[Attachment: initial-scope.md (text)]

—
Kimberly Park
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Letter of engagement: runtime interop & tracing co-development

Looping in Priya to validate dev/resource asks. Quick notes from infra:

- We will need one backend engineer (2 wks) and 0.5 FTE from runtime to expose a trace export hook and an opt-in flag for KV cache sampling.
- Ops needs a stubbed dataset and a clear scrub policy; Priya, can you confirm if the test VPC can host the replay harness?
- Billing: this looks like a partner engineering engagement — recommend a capped time-and-materials SOW; if Elliot needs deeper support we can convert to a paid pilot.

Priya — are you ok to take point on the scoping session and list preflight infra checks?

Jonas
From: Elijah Stone <elijah@elliot-consulting.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
